text:
maya: Heads-up — I prototyped a delegated-lease refactor for cross-site handoff. Trying to avoid the full escrow flow for small tenants. TL;DR: add a short-lived proxy-lease and a lease-accept hook.
jordan: curious, sketch? keep it lightweight pls, we already have operator surface area issues :grimacing:
maya: sure. idea: instead of forcing full escrow snapshot when moving primary, we issue a proxy-lease token that the receiving region can query to validate ownership. If accepted, region swaps in-place and claims KV ownership. If not accepted within TTL, original keeps it.
sam: sounds similar to the current lease-swap but with a 2-step validate/claim. what's the difference vs escrowed writes?
maya: escrow is heavy — snapshot + replay. Proxy-lease is just a signed capability referencing last-committed-seq + optional consent flags. No data movement until real writes happen.
elio: does this change client-visible semantics? i.e., could a write be accepted then lost if swap fails? we need strong guarantees for tenant billing and compliance.
maya: good call. plan: reads remain served by origin until claim completes. Writes will be gated by the claim check: if proxy-lease present, writes are forwarded to origin with a fast-ack path that logs a tombstone if claim fails later. We keep at-least-one durable path.
jordan: can you paste the proto/interface you had in mind for the hook? makes it easier to reason about compat.
maya: pasted below — very rough.
```
service LeaseCoordinator {
  rpc IssueProxyLease(ProxyLeaseRequest) returns (ProxyLeaseToken);
  rpc ValidateLease(TokenValidationRequest) returns (ValidationResponse);
  rpc ClaimLease(ClaimRequest) returns (ClaimResponse);
}

message ProxyLeaseToken { string token; int64 expires_at; string last_seq; repeated string consents; }
```
sam: Thanks. A couple concerns:
- TTL needs to be safely longer than GC/lag windows or we create thrash.
- Need audit log entries for every proxy issue and claim for compliance.
elio: also add a sync-safe fallback: if claim fails due to network partition, we must be able to rollback acceptances or honor eventual primary with monotonicity.
maya: agreed on both. Implementation notes I had:
- default TTL = 2m, operator-configurable up to 10m.
- token signed by originating region KMS; receiving region verifies signature and last_seq.
- ClaimResponse includes a conflict hint: {accepted, conflicting_seq, retry_after}
jordan: operator UX: how will this surface in the console? we need clear state: PENDING_PROXY / CLAIMED / REVOKED so oncall knows what's happening.
maya: console states mapped 1:1. ops-bot will post events during Issue/Claim with links to the tenant + trace id.
ops-bot: automsg — lease-proxy: issued for tenant=acme-corp ttl=120s trace=lkj-34
sam: testing plan: simnet chaos with induced cross-region partition; assert no data loss and that client-visible latencies stay within SLO during passive period.
elio: what about migrations mid-rolling-upgrade of runtime? binary compatibility with older control-plane that doesn't understand proxy-lease?
maya: fallback: if receiving region cannot validate token (old control-plane), we fall back to full escrow flow. This keeps compatibility but increases cost for older clusters.
jordan: okay. can you add a small perf model? when does proxy-lease pay off vs escrow (tenant QPS, average session length)?
maya: quick numbers I ran locally: for tenants < 50 qps and state size < 5MB, proxy-lease reduces cutover latency from ~12s to ~1.2s and network egress by ~95%. For high-QPS big-state tenants escrow still wins.
sam: neat. last ask: add a safety knob to disable proxy-lease per-tenant via feature flag (console + API). Compliance can opt out.
maya: yes — feature flag + operator override. I'll open a draft RFC and a small PR for coordinator proto + ops-bot hooks. Will copy tests and perf snippets in the RFC.
elio: thanks — please add the audit/event contract in the RFC (schema + retention). Also include failure-mode diagrams.
jordan: thanks team. @maya ping when you have the RFC link and a pre-merge design doc. :thumbsup:
